newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Probe blames Croat police over Mostar incident.
newsitem.headline: Probe blames Croat police over Mostar incident.

text.p: International police investigators reported on Tuesday that Bosnian Croat police fired on unarmed Moslems without cause and in a criminal manner in an incident this month in the divided town of Mostar.

"The use by law enforcement officers of excessive force in beating marchers, and of unnecessary and disproportionate lethal force, resulted in one death and numerous injuries," said the international police report, obtained by Reuters.

The investigation, conducted by a team of monitors from the International Police Task Force (IPTF), said two Croat police were seen firing into a crowd of retreating Moslems who had tried to visit a cemetery in Croat-held western Mostar.

One of the policemen was identified as Ivan Hrkac, deputy chief of police in western Mostar, the report said. The February 10 attack on the Moslem procession was the worst violence seen in Bosnia since a peace agreement was signed in December 1995.
Michael Steiner, deputy to the international High Representative to Bosnia, met leaders of the Moslem-Croat federation on Tuesday evening to discuss the report.
